title: Academic calendar and term dates
content: Term 1 teaching runs from 7 July 2026 through 23 October 2026. Reading week is 24 to 28 August. Term 2 teaching runs from 4 January 2027 through 19 March 2027. The calendar lists these dates as planning dates for the fictional institute.

title: Course registration window
content: Students register for Term 1 courses in the Northbridge student portal from 22 June to 3 July 2026. The programme office publishes the available section list before registration opens. Students who miss the window should email their programme office rather than create a duplicate registration request.

title: Add and drop period
content: The add and drop period stays open for the first seven calendar days of teaching, from 7 to 13 July 2026 for Term 1. A student may drop a course in the portal during this period without an academic penalty. After the period closes, the programme office must approve any exception.

title: Attendance and participation record
content: A course coordinator records attendance for scheduled teaching sessions. A student should contact the coordinator within two working days when illness or an approved activity prevents attendance. The corpus does not set one institute-wide attendance percentage; each course outline states its own participation rule.

title: Academic advising appointments
content: The Academic Advising Desk releases appointment slots every Monday at 09:00 through the student portal. Students can book one 20-minute appointment per week. Bring the current course plan and any registration error message to the meeting.

title: Grade appeal first step
content: A student who believes a marking error occurred should first request a written review from the course coordinator within ten working days of grade release. The request must name the assessment and the specific marking concern. A programme-level appeal is available only after this first review.

title: Examination timetable publication
content: The Examination Office publishes the final timetable in the student portal at least fourteen days before the first examination. Students must check the room, date, start time, and permitted materials for every paper. A timetable shown in a personal calendar is not the official schedule.

title: Examination eligibility check
content: The Examination Office checks eligibility after the course registration list closes. A student with an unresolved fee hold or missing course registration should contact the Registry before the timetable is published. Invigilators cannot add a student to the room list on the examination day.

title: Missed examination reporting
content: If illness or an emergency causes a student to miss an examination, the student should submit the Mitigating Circumstances form to the Examination Office within two working days. The form asks for the paper details and supporting evidence. The office then communicates the next available assessment route.

title: Revaluation request
content: A student may request a revaluation within five working days of receiving the final grade. The request goes to the Examination Office with the prescribed form and receipt. A revaluation can change the mark in either direction, so the original mark is not guaranteed.

title: Academic integrity during examinations
content: Students must bring their institute ID and follow the permitted-materials list for each paper. Unauthorised notes, devices, or communication count as an academic-integrity concern and are reported by the invigilator. The student should not argue about the report in the examination room.

title: Examination accommodations
content: Students who need examination accommodations should register with Accessibility Services at least fifteen working days before the first paper. Accessibility Services sends the approved arrangement to the Examination Office. Individual arrangements are not confirmed by an invigilator on the day.

title: Term fee payment dates
content: Term 1 fees are due by 31 July 2026 at 17:00. The finance portal accepts card and bank-transfer payments. A payment submitted after the deadline may take two working days to appear in the student account.

title: Late payment hold
content: A fee balance that remains unpaid after the due date places a temporary financial hold on the student account. The hold can block course registration and official transcript requests. Contact the Finance Desk with the payment reference if a paid balance still shows a hold after two working days.

title: Course withdrawal refund window
content: A student who withdraws during the first seven calendar days of teaching may request a full course-fee reversal for that course. The request must be submitted through the Finance Portal before the add and drop period closes. Accommodation and service charges follow separate terms that are not covered by this record.

title: Installment plan request
content: Students can request a three-part installment plan before the first fee deadline by submitting the plan form in the Finance Portal. The first installment is due on the normal deadline, and the Finance Desk confirms the later dates by email. An approved plan does not remove the need to register for courses.

title: Payment receipt and reference
content: The Finance Portal issues a receipt number after a payment is accepted. Students should save the receipt PDF and quote the receipt number in any Finance Desk query. Bank screenshots without a transaction reference may not be enough to match a payment.

title: Fee query escalation
content: For an incorrect charge, the student should open a Finance Portal query and attach the invoice or receipt within ten working days of the charge appearing. The Finance Desk replies to the portal ticket. Do not email card numbers or bank passwords to staff.

title: Library opening hours
content: The Northbridge Library is open Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 21:00 and Saturday from 10:00 to 16:00 during teaching weeks. It is closed on Sunday. Holiday hours are posted at the library entrance and are not included in this record.

title: Undergraduate borrowing limit
content: An undergraduate student may borrow up to six books at one time for a loan period of fourteen days. The library account shows the due date for each item. Reference-only items cannot leave the library.

title: Book renewal rule
content: A borrowed book can be renewed twice through the library catalogue if no other student has placed a reservation. Renewal starts a new fourteen-day period from the renewal date. A reserved item must be returned on its current due date.

title: Overdue item reminder
content: The library sends an automated reminder one day after a book becomes overdue. The synthetic policy does not charge a daily fine, but a student cannot borrow another item while an overdue item remains unresolved. Ask the library desk about a damaged or lost book.

title: Electronic resource access
content: Students access subscribed journals and databases through the Library Search page after signing in with their institute account. Off-campus access uses the library proxy link. The library desk can reset access after checking the student account.

title: Group study room booking
content: A student group can reserve a library study room for up to two hours per day through the library booking page. The booking must include the group size and a student contact. Groups that do not arrive within fifteen minutes can lose the reservation.

title: Merit scholarship eligibility
content: The fictional Northbridge Merit Scholarship is open to continuing students with a term average of at least 75 percent and no unresolved academic-integrity case. The award committee checks the official grade record after applications close. Meeting the threshold does not guarantee an award.

title: Need-based support grant
content: The Northbridge Need-Based Support Grant helps students who can document a change in household income or an essential study expense. Students submit the grant form and supporting documents to Student Support. The committee reviews evidence rather than using a single automatic income cutoff.

title: Scholarship application window
content: Applications for the Term 1 scholarship round open on 10 August 2026 and close on 28 August 2026 at 17:00. Late applications are not reviewed in that round. Student Support posts the decision date after the committee meeting.

title: Scholarship document checklist
content: A scholarship application should include the completed form, a current institute ID copy, the latest grade record, and the document requested for the selected award. Upload files as PDF documents through the Student Support Portal. The portal shows a missing-file warning before submission.

title: Scholarship award disbursement
content: Approved scholarship awards are credited to the student account after the committee decision and enrolment check. Student Support sends the expected credit date in the award message. The record does not promise a cash transfer to a personal bank account.

title: Emergency study support
content: A student facing an urgent study-related expense can request Emergency Study Support through the Student Support Portal. Explain the expense, amount, and timing, then attach any available evidence. A support adviser contacts the student if more information is needed.

title: Registering a student club
content: A new student club needs five currently enrolled student members, a faculty adviser, and a one-page constitution. Submit the registration packet to the Student Activities Office. The office reviews the name, purpose, and officer list before publishing the club directory.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Student Activities Guide 2026, C-01

title: Club activity funding
content: Registered clubs may request up to 12,000 Northbridge credits per term from the Student Activities Fund. The request must include a budget, event purpose, and expected attendance. Funds cannot pay personal travel or unapproved gifts.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Student Activities Guide 2026, C-02

title: Booking a club room
content: A registered club can book a student activity room through the Campus Spaces calendar at least three working days before the meeting. The booking officer must list the expected attendance and equipment. Room access ends at the time shown in the calendar.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Student Activities Guide 2026, C-03

title: Student event approval
content: A club event open to more than thirty attendees needs an Event Approval Form at least ten working days before the event. The form covers room, sound, accessibility, and safety arrangements. An event is not approved because a room calendar entry exists.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Student Activities Guide 2026, C-04

title: Joining a registered club
content: Any currently enrolled student may join a registered club by contacting the club officer listed in the student activity directory. Clubs may set reasonable activity expectations, but they cannot require a student to pay an unlisted membership charge. The directory shows the club contact channel.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Student Activities Guide 2026, C-05

title: Club conduct concern
content: A student who experiences harassment or unsafe conduct at a club activity can report it to Student Activities or the Safety Desk. Include the event name, date, and a safe contact method. The student does not need to confront the club officer before reporting.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Student Activities Guide 2026, C-06

title: Placement programme eligibility
content: A student may register for the Term 1 placement programme after completing at least 60 credits, maintaining a term average of 60 percent or higher, and clearing any fee hold. The Career Centre verifies the record before enabling applications.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Career Centre Guide 2026, P-01

title: Placement portal registration
content: Eligible students register on the Placement Portal between 1 and 14 August 2026. Upload a current resume and select the preferred work areas before submitting the registration. The Career Centre cannot submit a registration on a student's behalf.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Career Centre Guide 2026, P-02

title: Resume clinic booking
content: The Career Centre runs 25-minute resume clinics on Tuesdays and Thursdays during teaching weeks. Students book a slot through the Career Portal and should upload the draft resume at least one day before the appointment. Bring one target role or industry to the session.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Career Centre Guide 2026, P-03

title: Interview room booking
content: A student invited to a remote interview may reserve a quiet interview booth in the Career Centre up to five working days in advance. The booth provides a desk, chair, and wired internet. Students should test the interview platform before the appointment.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Career Centre Guide 2026, P-04

title: Internship credit request
content: A student who wants academic credit for an internship must submit the Internship Credit Request before the internship begins. The request needs the offer letter, work hours, supervisor contact, and faculty approval. Credit cannot be added after the placement has ended.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Career Centre Guide 2026, P-05

title: Recruiter communication rule
content: Recruiter messages sent through the Placement Portal should be answered through the portal so the Career Centre can record the application status. Do not share an institute password or identity document by email. Report a suspicious recruiter message to the Career Centre.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Career Centre Guide 2026, P-06

title: Campus Wi-Fi access
content: Connect to the NBT-Student network with the institute account username and password. The network asks for a sign-in again every thirty days. If the password works elsewhere but Wi-Fi fails, open an IT Help Desk ticket and include the device type, building, and time of failure.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Facilities and IT Guide 2026, I-01

title: Computing laboratory hours
content: The main computing laboratory is open Monday to Saturday from 07:00 to 22:00 during teaching weeks. Access requires an active institute ID. Lab assistants can help with approved course software, but they do not repair personal devices.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Facilities and IT Guide 2026, I-02

title: Accessibility request for facilities
content: Students can request an accessible classroom, route, or seating adjustment through Accessibility Services. Submit the request at least ten working days before the class when possible. Facilities and the programme office coordinate the change; students do not need to negotiate it with a lecturer alone.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Facilities and IT Guide 2026, I-03

title: Maker space induction
content: The Maker Space is available to students who complete the online safety induction and a short tool-specific briefing. Book a machine through the Maker Space calendar after the briefing. Personal projects must use approved materials and stay within the booked session.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Facilities and IT Guide 2026, I-04

title: Lost property report
content: Report a lost item through the Campus Services form and include the last known building, approximate time, and a description. Found items should be handed to the nearest reception desk. Do not include a full identity number in the public description.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Facilities and IT Guide 2026, I-05

title: Maintenance request
content: Students can report a broken fixture, water leak, lighting issue, or classroom fault through the Campus Services maintenance form. Add the building, room number, and a short description. For an immediate danger, use the Safety Desk number instead of waiting for a maintenance ticket.
source: Northbridge Synthetic Facilities and IT Guide 2026, I-06

title: Campus emergency contact
content: For an immediate campus emergency, call the Northbridge Safety Desk at 555-0147 from any phone. State the building, floor, and nature of the emergency, then follow the desk's instructions. This fictional number is for the prototype dataset and is not a real emergency service.

title: Non-urgent incident report
content: Report a non-urgent safety or conduct incident through the Campus Safety Form within two working days when possible. Include what happened, where, when, and a safe way to contact you. You may ask Safety Desk staff about confidential reporting options.

title: Building evacuation action
content: When an alarm sounds, stop work, leave by the nearest marked exit, and go to the assembly point shown on the building notice. Do not use lifts or return for personal items. A floor warden reports the area status to the Safety Desk.

title: After-hours building access
content: After 20:00, students may enter approved study buildings only with an active institute ID and the building's access permission. Do not hold a door open for an unknown person. Report a failed access reader to the Safety Desk or reception.

title: Counselling appointment
content: Students can request a confidential counselling appointment through Wellbeing Services using the Student Support Portal. The first appointment is an intake meeting that discusses the student's needs and available options. The portal does not display the reason for the request to teaching staff.

title: Lab safety induction
content: Students must complete the relevant lab safety induction before using a teaching laboratory or Maker Space. The induction record stays active for one academic year unless a supervisor assigns a refresher. Supervisors can deny access when the record is missing.
